messages:
michael: Heads-up — spotted a small but repeatable delta on the billing dashboard. A streaming request that got truncated + client retry ended up showing ~2x tokens in the session trace. logs attached below. :eyes:

jess: Can you paste the trace id? curious whether this is the retry path or a toolcall double-count.

michael: trace_id=txn-2026-04-12-99a3
billing-bot: provisional_charge emitted: session=txn-2026-04-12-99a3 tokens=236 state=provisional

michael: tl;dr: client opened stream, server sent chunk that was truncated due to max_tokens, client retried to resume, router took fallback path -> re-issued a toolcall. The toolcall returned quickly and stream resumed, but ledger shows both the provisional stream tokens and the toolcall tokens as confirmed. Looks like provisional didn't get revoked on resume fallback.

tara: hmm. that sequence rings a bell — we have code that converts provisional->confirmed on stream EOF, but truncated streams set EOF early and the resume flow may be skipping the provisional cancel. Might be a small state-machine gap.

sam: quick check: do we see duplicate token attribution keys? e.g. prefix_key vs toolcall_key both present?

michael: yes — payload has: prefix_key=pf_99a3 and toolcall_key=tc_99a3. Both mapped to confirmed bucket after resume.

jess: ugly but plausible. two immediate mitigations: 1) console: mark provisional as provisional in timeline UI (so ops can see it's pending) 2) server: make resume path explicitly revoke provisional entries when a fallback toolcall succeeds.

tara: agreed. for fix we should be conservative: when a resume route chooses a toolcall fallback, we should attach provenance: "supersedes: prefix_key" and then the ledger can dedupe. That avoids changing wide parts of billing.

sam: implementation note: internal API /ledger/confirm currently takes (session_id, tokens, tags). We can add optional supersedes_key param — simple and backward compatible.

michael: sample request we could emit: 
```
POST /ledger/confirm
{ "session_id": "txn-2026-04-12-99a3", "tokens": 120, "tags": ["stream","toolcall"], "supersedes": ["pf_99a3"] }
```

jess: +1. also add a small dashboard flag so provisional vs confirmed are filterable. ops frequently get pinged and right now they have to infer.

tara: telemetry question: do we have event that indicates "resume-via-toolcall" so we can query how often this pattern occurs? would help prioritize.

michael: there is a route_event but we don't currently surface the resume_reason. I propose emitting route_event with reason: resume|client_reconnect|fallback_toolcall. cheap change in router.

sam: sounds safe. we'll add unit test for ledger confirm with supersedes to ensure no double-count. Also add end-to-end in staging to validate dashboard metrics.

jess: plan: 1) sam adds supersedes param + tests 2) router emits resume reason + provenance on confirm 3) console adds provisional filter (small UX tweak) 4) run staging week and validate with synthetic replay of txn-2026-04-12-99a3 sequence.

michael: timeline? this is annoying ops but low severity. can we aim for a quick patch early next week?

sam: I'll slot a 1-day PR Monday, staging validate Tuesday.

tara: I'll file a tiny docs note about ledger supersedes and the console filter so support can explain to customers.

jess: great. leaving a follow-up action: if after staging we still see >1% of resumed streams double-counting in a week, we escalate to rollbackable hotfix. :+1:

michael: thanks everyone. tagging @support to FYI so they don't chase duplicates in the meantime.

billing-bot: note: created investigation ticket INV-2026-44 for trace txn-2026-04-12-99a3
